scope: All nine current standard Build Your Skills videos, 31 minutes 28 seconds in total. Sources are the installed files referenced by the current local course.
method: Sequentially decoded all nine installed videos and matched every reported frame count. Visually inspected all 20 six-second contact sheets and three closer scene sequences. Read fresh full-file timestamped transcripts for all nine, current lesson context, and relevant prior review/build records. Automated transcription can misrecognize wording. This is a visual-and-transcript audit, not continuous audiovisual viewing or a new factual certification.
recommendation: Build three focused updates: Maya’s interrupted contribution, a basketball team changing its play, and a student delivering on a community commitment. Keep four videos as they are; defer the opener pending its narration work; Know the App has a newer narration-approved roll and is now in production.

opportunities.title: Let us see the moment Maya goes quiet
opportunities.cue: Maya goes quiet and the group moves on. You notice that Maya’s expression and body language changed. What would you say or do next?
opportunities.current: Drawn students and an interruption diagram establish the story. Small invented project labels compete with the social interaction. Maya’s withdrawal is shown separately from the group.
opportunities.proposal: Follow one consistent group at a history-project table: satisfaction with the finished work, Maya trying to contribute, and Maya becoming quiet after being interrupted. Keep the other students in view so the change in participation is visible. Match Maya and the classmate to the existing photographic Your Next Move board.
opportunities.benefit: Gives the learner observable behavior to notice before the invitation on the next board. The lesson becomes a recognizable interaction rather than an explanation of an interaction.
beats: 0:00–0:08: establish the finished project and the group’s satisfaction.
0:08–0:15: Maya starts to point out something; another student interrupts. Reveal the short spoken interruption only when it is said.
0:15–0:26.6: same table and camera relationship; Maya stops contributing. Hold the decision moment, then cut to the existing invitation board.
opportunities.treatment: A small sequence of photographic stills with restrained camera movement, not one 27-second still. Maintain people, clothing, seating, project and eyelines across states. Do not assign Maya an unspoken emotion or restore the previously removed “She seems hurt” line. Use generic project pages without invented historical mistakes. Render any exact interruption text separately. Preserve the later scene where her idea improves the project.
opportunities.board: Preserve Your Next Move beginning at 0:26.60, its invitation and banner highlights, all Four Ways and Matter More boards, the useful Notice/Ask and Challenge Ideas diagrams, and the close. Existing owner-approved narration exceptions remain.
opportunities.success: The learner can identify the change in Maya’s participation and a respectful next move without being told what she must be feeling.

opportunities.title: Make the blocked basketball play tangible
opportunities.cue: First, you have to be curious enough to actively look for a better play. Second, you must be flexible enough to stop relying on the old one, even if you know it by heart.
opportunities.current: A basketball-court process diagram uses small circles, a block, route arrows and abstract mindset labels. The logic is useful, but the opening asks learners to imagine being the captain while showing almost no human action.
opportunities.proposal: Use the same school team and court through three clear states: a familiar passing lane, a defender closing that lane, and the captain spotting an open teammate and choosing a different pass. Retain a small, simple court inset only where it helps show which route changed.
opportunities.benefit: Separates looking for another option from actually abandoning the old play. The basketball analogy becomes concrete before the video transfers it to changing AI workflows.
beats: 0:00–0:10: establish the captain, teammates and familiar route in a school gym.
0:10–0:19: show the defender blocking that route. Keep court positions consistent.
0:19–0:30.37: emphasize the open alternative on “curious,” then the changed choice on “flexible.” Return to the existing update scene as the narration transfers the analogy to AI.
opportunities.treatment: Three or four coherent photographic states with minimal separately rendered route overlays; avoid a single long hold or a busy sports montage. Use “Curious: look for another play” and “Flexible: change the play” only on their matching cues. Do not add a new score, a guaranteed-success badge, or a made basket. The existing exit is frame 911 (0:30.37); preserve that transition and duration.
opportunities.board: Keep Stay Curious and Be Flexible, all existing interface cutaways about updates, newsletters, familiar work and comparison, the repaired final process diagram, and the close. This proposal touches only the opening analogy.
opportunities.success: At normal speed, the learner can distinguish discovering an alternative from switching to it, and the photos and route inset agree about player positions.

opportunities.title: Finish on a student delivering something that matters
opportunities.cue: Put yourself in a position where you are responsible for delivering a result that matters to other people.
opportunities.current: A donation-drive drawing shows a leader pointing beside boxes and a row of volunteers. It names the setting but mostly depicts people waiting for direction.
opportunities.proposal: Keep the existing donation-drive example and show the work underway: a student coordinator checks a short collection list as teammates sort supplies and hand over a packed box. Give the result a clear focal point—the prepared box being delivered—rather than a person pointing.
opportunities.benefit: Makes responsibility visible as follow-through and a result for others, giving the course’s final action advice a concrete human example.
beats: Establish the student coordinating the drive and checking progress.
Use a restrained push toward the handoff of a completed box while the narration says “delivering a result.”
opportunities.treatment: One carefully composed photographic scene is enough for roughly six seconds. Avoid invented donation totals, charity branding, readable personal information, or a new problem requiring explanation. Preserve the original close entrance; use existing shot edges at frames 8167–8343 (4:32.23–4:38.10).
opportunities.board: Preserve all six career examples and their photographic cutaways, Four Skills to Build, the owner’s Create and Solve title, the four action cards, and the full final takeaway. Replace only the existing donation-drive supporting shot.
opportunities.success: The learner sees a student taking responsibility for an actual completed task, and can read that action in the brief interval before the close.
